cover.headline: India's beauty leader is accelerating and finally profitable, but the price already pays for it
cover.lead: Nykaa is India's largest specialist beauty retailer (app, website and 324 stores), owns a fast-growing set of beauty brands, runs a premium fashion platform and supplies small shops through Superstore. At ₹{{P.last|num}} the stock is 7% below its 52-week high and ~70% above its bonus-adjusted IPO price of ₹187.5. Q1FY27 was its best quarter in years: revenue +29%, EBITDA +68%, Beauty growing 29% at a 10.3% margin and Fashion at breakeven. But at ~₹91,691 cr the market already pays ~43x Beauty's Sep-28E EBITDA. Our sum of the parts gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}})**: **we initiate with HOLD.** Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}} ({{scen.bear.upside|chg}}).

arguments.h: Beauty: the profitable leader, growing faster again
arguments.p: Beauty GMV rose 28% in Q1FY27 (NSV +29%; group revenue growth was the fastest in 13 quarters) at a 10.3% EBITDA margin on NSV. Owned brands (House of Nykaa, ₹1,700 cr of NSV in FY26) and premium global brands lift the gross margin; 324 stores add reach. We assume 25-27% GMV growth, the low end of the FY30 ambition.

arguments.h: Fashion has turned the corner, but is not yet a profit engine
arguments.p: Fashion GMV +53% in Q1FY27 and EBITDA at breakeven for a second quarter, after a ₹93 cr loss in FY25, as marketing fell from 28% to 23% of NSV. The Nike partnership (from Feb-2026) flatters growth until Q4FY27. We value Fashion at 1.5x Sep-28E GMV.

arguments.h: Profit is finally scaling, with almost no dilution
arguments.p: EBITDA +68% and profit ₹80 cr in Q1FY27; cash from operations ₹644 cr in FY26 against capex of ₹154 cr. ESOP cost was only ₹17 cr in FY26, unlike most Indian internet peers. But depreciation, interest and a 38% tax rate leave net profit at ~3% of revenue, so EPS stays small: {{F.eps.0|n2}} in FY27E.

arguments.h: Valuation: fair, with the target just short of a Buy
arguments.p: Our sum of the parts (Beauty 50x Sep-28E EBITDA, the street's median; Fashion 1.5x GMV) gives {{dcf.tp|inr}}, {{dcf.upside|chg}}. With Fashion at our value, the price implies ~43x Beauty's Sep-28E EBITDA. Our DCF at a 12.5% cost of equity gives only ₹184: the street multiples assume very long, fast growth. Street median target ₹398.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): does Beauty hold its 29% NSV growth with the festive season shifting (flagged on the Q1 call), and does Superstore's GST-led price drag fade as management expects from Q3?
Fashion: growth once the Nike partnership enters the base (mid-Q4FY27), and whether EBITDA stays positive.
Quick commerce: Blinkit, Zepto, Instamart and Flipkart Minutes adding beauty; Nykaa Now (60-minute delivery) is Nykaa's answer.
Store roll-out toward ~600 by FY30 (324 now) and the closing of the Aminu Wellness purchase (expected Q2FY27).

sections.title: A beauty retailer with its own brands, plus a fashion platform

blocks.p: Nykaa (the listed company is FSN E-Commerce Ventures) sells beauty and personal-care products through its app, website and 324 stores, and fashion through Nykaa Fashion. In Beauty it mostly **buys and sells the goods itself** (it owns the inventory), so revenue is close to the value of what it sells; in Fashion it is mainly a **marketplace** earning a commission, so revenue is a small share of the value of goods sold. It reports three measures: **GMV** (gross merchandise value, the price of goods ordered before discounts, returns and taxes), **NSV** (net sales value, after them) and revenue. Since FY26 it reports two verticals: Beauty (which now includes the Superstore eB2B arm and owned brands) and Fashion.

blocks.callout: **Why value Beauty on EBITDA and Fashion on GMV?** Beauty earns 9.6% of NSV (FY26) and its profit is the thing to value: we use 50x Sep-28E EBITDA, the street's median. Fashion has only just reached breakeven, so an EBITDA multiple would be meaningless; we value its order flow (GMV) at 1.5x, the median of the two broker values that were disclosed.

sections.title: From a 2021 IPO darling to a 70% fall, and back above the IPO price

blocks.p: Nykaa listed in November 2021 at the peak of India's internet boom: the IPO was priced at ₹1,125 and the stock opened ~78% higher. A 5:1 bonus issue in November 2022 multiplied the share count by six (equity capital rose from ₹47 cr to ₹285 cr), so every per-share number before then must be divided by six: the IPO price is ₹187.5 on today's basis. The stock then fell ~70% from its listing-month high to ~₹121 in April 2023 (weekly closes), as pre-IPO investors sold after their lock-ins expired, profits stayed tiny and the market turned against loss-making or barely profitable internet stocks. It has since recovered to ₹320 as growth re-accelerated and margins rose.

sections.title: Beauty: a $23bn market growing 12% a year, and online twice as fast

blocks.p: India's beauty and personal-care (BPC) market was about $23bn in FY26 and is expected to grow 12%+ a year to ~$42bn by FY31 (by then the fourth-largest in the world), according to Redseer research presented at Nykaa's June 2026 Investor Day. Online is growing 20%+ a year. Growth comes from more urban households, skincare routines spreading beyond the big cities and "premiumisation" (people trading up to costlier brands). Fashion is a much bigger market, where online grows ~22-25% a year and premium online fashion is expected to roughly triple by FY31. These are the company's own commissioned forecasts: useful for direction, optimistic by design.

bullets: **Reliance (Tira)**: deep-pocketed omnichannel beauty retailer with its own stores and app; the main specialist rival.
**Myntra (Flipkart)**: sells both fashion and beauty to a much larger fashion customer base; Nykaa Fashion's main rival.
**Amazon, Purplle and brand-owned websites (D2C)**: compete on mass and mid-priced beauty.

**Quick-commerce apps** (Blinkit, Zepto, Swiggy Instamart, Flipkart Minutes): deliver mass beauty in 10-30 minutes. Elara (25-Aug-2026) argues Nykaa's curated range and higher order values (₹2,102 in Beauty) protect it; Nykaa launched Nykaa Now (60-minute delivery in 13 cities) and says it does not discount from its own pocket.

blocks.callout: **So what:** the market is large and growing, and Nykaa is the specialist leader. But it is not a winner-takes-all market: brands sell everywhere, and the same lipstick is available on Tira, Myntra, Amazon and Blinkit at a price the brand sets. Nykaa wins on choice (10,000+ brands), authenticity, content and exclusive launches, not on price.

sections.title: Does the beauty boom reach Nykaa? Yes: it is growing ~2x the market

blocks.p: If the BPC market grows ~12% a year and online ~20%, a specialist that grows Beauty GMV at 28% (Q1FY27) and 27% (FY26) is gaining share. HSIE (22-Jun-2026) points out that part of FY24-26 growth came from two tailwinds that will fade: House of Nykaa (~60% a year, helped by the Dot & Key purchase) and Superstore (~41% a year); core Beauty grew ~22%. So the tailwind is real, but our forecast of 25-27% GMV growth asks core Beauty to keep beating the online market.

sections.title: Beauty: growing 28% at a 10.3% margin, with owned brands doing the heavy lifting

blocks.p: Beauty is ~75% of GMV and all of Nykaa's profit. It combines the Nykaa app and website (most of the business), 324 stores, the House of Nykaa brands (Nykaa Cosmetics, Kay Beauty, Dot & Key and others: ₹1,700 cr of NSV in FY26, ~16% of group GMV), Superstore (eB2B supply to small shops) and Nykaa Man grooming. In Q1FY27 GMV rose 28% to ₹4,105 cr on more buyers (annual unique customers +25% to 20.8 mn) and slightly bigger baskets (AOV +5% to ₹2,102). The EBITDA margin rose to 10.3% of NSV from 9% a year earlier.

blocks.p: Where the margin comes from: the gross margin is up ~1.5pp in two years (owned brands earn more than third-party brands; premium brands; brands paying for advertising on the app), and overheads have fallen as a share of sales. Fulfilment and marketing have stayed roughly flat: Nykaa is reinvesting in faster delivery (Nykaa Now) and customer acquisition. That is a healthy mix: the gains are structural, not from cutting growth spending.

blocks.p: Superstore supplies beauty and personal-care products to 523k registered small retailers (chemists, general stores) in 1,200+ cities. GMV was ~₹1,187 cr in FY26 and ₹336 cr in Q1FY27 (+17%; NSV +28%, as GST cuts lowered retail prices). Nykaa stopped reporting its profit when it merged Superstore into Beauty in FY26; HSIE estimates an EBITDA loss of ~7% of NSV in FY26. Management targets ₹3,500 cr of GMV and breakeven by FY30. Our Beauty margin forecast includes these losses, which is one reason we add only ~0.4pp of GMV a year.

blocks.callout: **Our forecast:** Beauty GMV +27% / +26% / +25% in FY27-29E and EBITDA of 6.0% / 6.4% / 6.8% of GMV (≈10.4% / 11.1% / 11.8% of NSV), giving Sep-28E EBITDA of ₹1,783 cr, which we value at 50x.

sections.title: Fashion: GMV +53% and at breakeven, but still a long way from Beauty's margins

blocks.p: Nykaa Fashion is a curated, premium fashion platform: mostly a marketplace, so revenue was only 16.8% of GMV in FY26. For years it grew slowly and lost money (EBITDA -₹93 cr in FY25, -8.3% of NSV). That has changed fast: GMV growth rose from 12% (FY25) to 30% (FY26) and 53% in Q1FY27, while marketing fell from 31% of NSV (FY25) to 23% (Q1FY27), so EBITDA reached breakeven in Q4FY26 and Q1FY27. Management credits a richer brand line-up (130+ new brands in Q1), cheaper customer acquisition (~30% lower cost per new customer in two years) and more repeat buyers.

bullets: **Nike is a boost, not the whole story.** Since Feb-2026 Nykaa runs Nike.in and the Nike app in India (1.5 mn+ app installs in six months). JM Financial asked on the Q1 call how growth looks once Nike enters the base in mid-Q4FY27; management said Q1 growth was "largely reflective of the underlying platform" and kept its 3-3.5x-by-FY30 guidance.
**Customers:** visits +28%, annual buyers +38% to 4.7 mn and orders +48% in Q1FY27; AOV fell 2% to ₹4,414, likely because men's (+83% GMV) and kids' (+57%) categories grew fastest.
**Competition:** Myntra (Flipkart) is the online fashion leader; Ajio (Reliance), Amazon and brand websites compete too. Nykaa Fashion is a niche premium player, not a leader.

blocks.callout: **Our forecast:** GMV +42% / +32% / +30% in FY27-29E and EBITDA of 0.3% / 0.9% / 1.5% of GMV (≈1% / 3% / 5% of NSV, short of the high-single-digit FY30 target). We value Fashion at 1.5x Sep-28E GMV (₹10,679 cr): ₹56 a share.

blocks.source: Nykaa presentations, MOFSL (4-Aug-2026), Elara (25-Aug-2026), GAM Research

blocks.callout: **Verdict: a narrow moat in Beauty.** Nykaa's edge is curation, trust and brand relationships, plus a growing owned-brand business, which together explain why it keeps ~10% margins while growing ~28%. It is not a monopoly: brands sell everywhere and rivals with deeper pockets (Reliance, Flipkart, Amazon, the quick-commerce apps) are investing in beauty. Fashion has no moat yet. Our 50x Beauty multiple assumes the moat holds; if quick commerce compresses Beauty growth to ~20%, our bear case applies.

sections.title: Revenue up 4x in five years; profit finally scaling

blocks.p: Nykaa's revenue rose from ₹2,441 cr in FY21 to ₹10,022 cr in FY26 (33% a year), and growth has sped up again: +26% in FY26 and +29% in Q1FY27, the fastest in 13 quarters. Unlike most Indian internet companies, Nykaa has made a profit every year since FY21, but it was tiny until recently: profit attributable to shareholders was ₹19 cr in FY23 and ₹32 cr in FY24, as stores, warehouses, Fashion and the eB2B arm (Superstore) absorbed the profit from beauty. FY26 was the break-out year: EBITDA +59% to ₹752 cr and profit to ₹199 cr. Q1FY27 added EBITDA +68% and profit ₹80 cr.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** the margin gains are real and come from three places: a higher gross margin (45.9% of revenue in Q1FY27 vs 44.6% a year earlier, from owned brands, premium brands and advertising income from brands), lower marketing as a share of sales in Fashion, and overheads growing slower than revenue. But reported net profit is still only 2.9% of revenue, because depreciation (3.2% of revenue, including leased stores), interest (~1%) and a high tax rate (38%) sit between EBITDA and earnings. That is why the P/E looks so high.

sections.title: Earnings quality: clean accounts, but a high tax rate and a minority to buy out

blocks.p: Nykaa's accounts are straightforward for an Indian internet company: it reports EBITDA as profit before tax plus interest and depreciation, less other income, and its vertical EBITDA adds up exactly to that number (FY26: ₹819 cr Beauty, ₹-37 cr Fashion, ₹-30 cr others = ₹752 cr). Share-based pay is inside EBITDA and is small (₹16.7 cr in FY26). Five things still need care.

bullets: **Rent sits below EBITDA.** Under Ind AS 116, store and warehouse rent shows up as depreciation of right-of-use assets and interest on lease liabilities (₹491 cr at Mar-26), not as an operating cost. EBITDA therefore overstates cash profit; we deduct lease liabilities as debt in our valuation.

**A minority to buy out.** Nykaa owns 51% of Dot & Key and has promised to buy the other 49% (a put option). The liability was revalued from ₹136 cr to ₹270 cr in FY26 as Dot & Key grew; it is booked in equity, not the P&L. Minorities took ₹4.5 cr of FY26 profit, so profit attributable to shareholders was ₹199 cr, not the ₹204 cr headline.

**High tax rate.** Tax was 38% of profit before tax in FY26 and Q1FY27, because profits in the parent are taxed at ~25% while losses in subsidiaries (Fashion, others) cannot be set off. The rate should fall as Fashion turns profitable; we assume 35% / 32% / 30%.

**Advertising income inside revenue.** Brands pay Nykaa to promote products on its app; management cites "marketing income" as one driver of the gross-margin gain. It is high-margin but depends on brands' marketing budgets.

**Less disclosure after resegmentation.** Since FY26 Superstore (eB2B), which loses money, is reported inside Beauty, so investors can no longer see its losses. An exceptional charge of ₹17.4 cr was taken in FY26.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** No sign of aggressive accounting: S.R. Batliboi gave a clean opinion, adjusted metrics reconcile and dilution is tiny. Amber because rent is below EBITDA, the put option grows with Dot & Key's success, and the eB2B losses are now out of sight.

sections.title: Balance sheet: small net debt, funded by suppliers and short-term loans

blocks.p: Nykaa holds ₹320 cr of cash and bank balances (Mar-26) against ₹747 cr of bank borrowings (almost all short-term working-capital loans) and ₹491 cr of lease liabilities on stores and warehouses: net debt of ₹918 cr including leases, or ₹427 cr without them. The business needs inventory (₹1,642 cr at Mar-26: it buys much of what it sells in Beauty), partly funded by suppliers (trade payables ₹732 cr). Cash from operations turned solidly positive in FY25 (₹467 cr) and FY26 (₹644 cr), and capex is light (₹154 cr in FY26), so free cash flow now covers the business; the company repaid debt in FY25-FY26 (cash from financing negative).

sections.title: Ownership: the Nayar family controls 52%; Indian funds are the next-largest owners

blocks.p: The Nayar family controls Nykaa through six family trusts holding 52.1%, unchanged over the past year. Indian funds (24.1%) own almost twice as much as foreign investors (13.7%): SBI Contra Fund is the largest single fund holder at 4.2%.

blocks.p: Our read: a founder who has built and run the business for 14 years, with two of her children now running Beauty and the owned brands and professional CEOs in Fashion and Superstore. The board has an independent majority and the auditor is a large firm. The main governance question is succession and family influence, not honesty: the auditor's opinion on the FY26 accounts is unmodified and we saw no accounting concerns.

sections.title: Our forecasts: EBITDA nearly triples by FY29E; EPS grows faster

blocks.p: We build the forecast vertical by vertical. Each vertical's GMV (revenue for the small GCC business) grows at our assumed rate; revenue and EBITDA are a % of GMV. Group EBITDA is the sum of the verticals, as Nykaa reports it. Below EBITDA, depreciation is a % of gross block (including leased stores), interest covers leases and working-capital loans, and tax falls from 35% to 30% as Fashion turns profitable.

We are a little behind the plan on purpose: Q1FY27 margins were boosted by Fashion's sudden turn, and quick commerce is a live threat in mass beauty.

blocks.p: After Q1FY27 the street turned almost uniformly positive: 6 of 8 brokers with a post-Q1 call rate Nykaa a Buy or Outperform, on faster Beauty growth, the Fashion turnaround and margin expansion. MOFSL (Neutral, ₹370) likes the business but calls valuation "a key deterrent". Before the results, HSIE was at Sell (₹220, DCF), arguing that the FY30 ambitions are lofty. The median post-Q1 target is ₹398. Brokers that disclose a method use a sum of the parts (MOFSL, Nuvama, Elara) or a DCF (JM Financial, HSIE); Beauty is valued at 45-60x EV/EBITDA or 75x P/E (Elara), Fashion at a DCF value (MOFSL ₹24,900 cr) or 4x sales (Elara).

blocks.callout: Cross-checks: the DCF (12.5% cost of equity, 6% terminal growth, margin rising to 15%) gives ₹184 (−49% vs our SOTP). That gap is the honest bear case: a 50x EBITDA multiple prices in fast growth for well over a decade. EV/EBITDA at 50x Sep-28E group EBITDA gives ₹327 (−10%): Fashion's GMV is worth more than its still-small EBITDA. Each 5x on Beauty is worth ~₹31 a share; each 0.5x of Fashion GMV ~₹19.

blocks.p: We value each business on our Sep-28E forecasts (the average of FY28E and FY29E), deduct the net debt (including lease liabilities, because segment EBITDA is before rent) we expect at March 2027, and deduct the value of the Dot & Key minority that Nykaa has agreed to buy. Every input is live in the SOTP sheet of the Excel model, with Base / Bull / Bear switches.

bullets: **Beauty (BPC):** Median of the three EV/EBITDA multiples the street disclosed by 30-Sep-2026 (MOSL 50x FY28E Beauty EBITDA; JM Financial's DCF target implies 45x FY29E EBITDA; HSIE's DCF target implies 60x Jun-28E EBITDA, pre-Q1) = 50x. Bull 60x (HSIE-implied), bear 45x (JM-implied). Applied to Sep-28E Beauty EBITDA, which is after Superstore (eB2B) losses and before rent.

**Fashion:** Two brokers disclosed a Fashion value: MOSL's DCF ₹24,900 cr (₹87/share) and Elara's 4x sales, which on our Sep-28E Fashion revenue is ~₹7,300 cr. Their median (₹16,100 cr) = 1.5x our Sep-28E GMV. Bull 2.3x (MOSL), bear 0.7x (Elara). GMV rather than EBITDA because Fashion has just reached breakeven, so an EBITDA multiple is meaningless.
**Others (GCC, international):** Start-up losses valued as the cost still to come: three years of FY28E losses (bull one, bear five), as for Eternal's and Swiggy's new bets.

**Net debt at end-FY27E (incl. leases):** Model forecast: cash and bank less working-capital borrowings and lease liabilities at Mar-27. Leases are deducted because segment EBITDA is before rent (Ind AS 116).

**Dot & Key minority (put option):** Beauty is valued at 100%, but 49% of Dot & Key belongs to its founders and Nykaa has written a put option to buy it; the liability was ₹269.5 cr at Mar-26 (FY26 annual report, note 53A). Other minorities (Earth Rhythm ~25%) are immaterial (minority profit ₹4.5 cr in FY26).

sections.title: Our honest summary: a better business than the 2023 market thought, at a price that already says so

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** India's leading specialist beauty retailer (Beauty GMV +28% at a 10.3% margin on NSV), a portfolio of owned brands, and a Fashion business that has just reached breakeven, for a market value of ~₹91,691 cr. Our sum of the parts gives {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}).

**What you are paying for:** with Fashion at our value, ~43x Beauty's Sep-28E EBITDA (we use 50x, the street's median), or ~103x our Sep-28E EPS. Our DCF at a 12.5% cost of equity gives only ₹184: to justify today's price on cash flows you need fast growth for 15+ years. If quick commerce slows Beauty to ~21% and Fashion stalls (our bear case), the stock is worth {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

**Sell above ~₹385**, or if Beauty NSV growth falls below 20% for two quarters (the quick-commerce risk showing up).
**Position size:** a market weight; the business deserves to be owned, but the margin of safety is thin and the DCF gap is wide.

exhibit.title: Terms used in this report
head: Term
Meaning
rows: Gross merchandise value: the price of goods ordered, before discounts, cancellations, returns and taxes.
Net sales value: GMV after discounts, cancellations, returns and taxes. Nykaa quotes vertical margins as a % of NSV.
Sales of goods Nykaa owns plus commissions, advertising and logistics income. Close to NSV in Beauty (inventory model), much smaller in Fashion (marketplace).
Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation; at Nykaa, after share-based pay and before store rent (Ind AS 116).
Gross profit less fulfilment, marketing and selling costs, as a % of NSV.
Average order value; annual unique transacting customers.
Nykaa's owned brands: Nykaa Cosmetics, Kay Beauty, Dot & Key, Earth Rhythm and others.
Nykaa's business supplying beauty products to small retailers via an app (electronic business-to-business).
Apps delivering groceries and household goods in 10-30 minutes from small local warehouses (Blinkit, Zepto, Instamart).
Valuing each business separately and adding them up, less net debt and minorities.
Enterprise value (market value plus net debt) divided by EBITDA or by GMV.
The average of our FY28E and FY29E forecasts, i.e. the twelve months to September 2028: the earnings a buyer will look at in a year.
A promise to buy the remaining 49% of Dot & Key from its founders, booked as a liability (₹270 cr at Mar-26).
The accounting rule that moves rent on leased stores and warehouses below EBITDA (into depreciation and interest).
Discounted cash flow: the value today of future free cash flows, discounted at the cost of capital.
